title: Risks for human health related to the presence of 3- and 2-monochloropropanediol (MCPD), and their fatty acid esters, and glycidyl fatty acid esters in food
authors: EFSA Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain (CONTAM)
funder: European Food Safety Authority, on request from the European Commission (Question number EFSA-Q-2014-00535).
result: 3- and 2-MCPD fatty acid esters are produced in vegetable oils on refining; glycidyl esters form from diacylglycerols when oils are heated above 200 °C, for example during deodorisation. Mean middle-bound concentrations (µg/kg) of 3-MCPD from esters: sunflower seed oil 521, maize oil 503, soya bean oil 394, rapeseed oil 232, palm oil/fat 2,912; of glycidol from esters: sunflower 269, maize 650, soya bean 171, rapeseed 166, palm 3,955. Glycidol increased tumour incidence in several tissues of rats and mice, likely via a genotoxic mode of action. Animal studies show extensive hydrolysis of esterified 3-MCPD and glycidol after oral administration; with no in vivo data for glycidyl esters, dose-response considerations assumed complete hydrolysis of the esters to free glycidol after ingestion. There is strong evidence from in vitro data and some evidence from in vivo studies that glycidol is genotoxic.
